chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Abbas, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who threw the Jamarat (stones) while he was riding, and he said, 'There is no harm in it.' And that which indicates that walking in it is superior is what he narrated.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to throw the Jamarat stones while riding a camel or horse during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the permissibility of throwing the Jamarat while mounted, a practical concession for pilgrims facing crowds or physical difficulty, yet affirms that walking remains the superior act of worship (afdhal). It reflects the Shia juristic principle of distinguishing between validity (sahih) and excellence (kamal) in ritual acts, emphasizing that ease does not negate the merit of the more arduous form. This ruling is foundational in the chapter on returning to Mina and is often cited alongside other narrations detailing the specific etiquette of the stoning ritual.
